     5	
     6	# Report Generator
     7	
     8	Create professional, data-driven reports with charts, tables, and narrative text. Perfect for business reports, analytics dashboards, status updates, and automated reporting pipelines.
     9	
    10	## Quick Start
    11	
    12	```python
    13	from scripts.report_gen import ReportGenerator
    14	
    15	# Create a simple report
    16	report = ReportGenerator("Monthly Sales Report")
    17	report.add_text("This report summarizes sales performance for Q4 2024.")
    18	report.add_table(sales_data, title="Sales by Region")
    19	report.add_chart(sales_data, chart_type="bar", title="Revenue by Month")
    20	report.add_text("Key findings: Revenue increased 25% quarter-over-quarter.")
    21	report.generate().save("sales_report.pdf")
    22	
    23	# From template
    24	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("executive_summary")
    25	report.set_data(data_dict)
    26	report.generate().save("exec_summary.pdf")
    27	```
    28	
    29	## Features
    30	
    31	- **Multiple Output Formats**: PDF, HTML
    32	- **Rich Content**: Text, tables, charts, images, headers
    33	- **Chart Types**: Bar, line, pie, scatter, area, heatmap
    34	- **Table Formatting**: Auto-styling, conditional formatting
    35	- **Templates**: Pre-built report templates
    36	- **Branding**: Logo, colors, fonts, headers/footers
    37	- **Sections**: Table of contents, page numbers, appendices
    38	- **Data Integration**: CSV, DataFrame, dict inputs
    39	
    40	## API Reference
    41	
    42	### Initialization
    43	
    44	```python
    45	# New report
    46	report = ReportGenerator("Report Title")
    47	report = ReportGenerator("Report Title", subtitle="Q4 2024 Analysis")
    48	
    49	# From template
    50	report = ReportGenerator.from_template("quarterly_review")
    51	
    52	# With config
    53	report = ReportGenerator("Title", config={
    54	    "page_size": "letter",
    55	    "orientation": "portrait",
    56	    "margins": {"top": 1, "bottom": 1, "left": 0.75, "right": 0.75}
    57	})
    58	```
    59	
    60	### Report Metadata
    61	
    62	```python
    63	# Title and subtitle
    64	report.set_title("Annual Report 2024")
    65	report.set_subtitle("Financial Performance Analysis")
    66	
    67	# Author and date
    68	report.set_author("Analytics Team")
    69	report.set_date("December 2024")
    70	report.set_date_auto()  # Use today
    71	
    72	# Organization
    73	report.set_organization("Acme Corporation")
    74	report.set_logo("logo.png")
    75	```
    76	
    77	### Adding Content
    78	
    79	#### Text Content
    80	
    81	```python
    82	# Simple paragraph
    83	report.add_text("This is a paragraph of analysis text.")
    84	
    85	# Styled text
    86	report.add_text("Important finding!", style="highlight")
    87	report.add_text("Key metric: 42%", style="metric")
    88	
    89	# Headers
    90	report.add_heading("Executive Summary", level=1)
    91	report.add_heading("Revenue Analysis", level=2)
    92	report.add_heading("By Region", level=3)
    93	
    94	# Bullet points
    95	report.add_bullets([
    96	    "Revenue increased 25% YoY",
    97	    "Customer acquisition up 15%",
    98	    "Churn rate decreased to 3%"
    99	])
   100	
   101	# Numbered list
   102	report.add_numbered_list([
   103	    "Expand to European markets",
   104	    "Launch mobile application",
   105	    "Implement AI-driven analytics"
   106	])
   107	```
   108	
   109	#### Tables
   110	
   111	```python
   112	# From DataFrame
   113	import pandas as pd
   114	df = pd.DataFrame({
   115	    'Region': ['North', 'South', 'East', 'West'],
   116	    'Revenue': [100000, 85000, 92000, 78000],
   117	    'Growth': ['12%', '8%', '15%', '5%']
   118	})
   119	report.add_table(df, title="Regional Performance")
   120	
   121	# From dict/list
   122	data = [
   123	    {'Product': 'A', 'Sales': 1000, 'Profit': 200},
   124	    {'Product': 'B', 'Sales': 1500, 'Profit': 350}
   125	]
   126	report.add_table(data, title="Product Summary")
   127	
   128	# With styling
   129	report.add_table(df, title="Sales Data",
   130	    highlight_max=['Revenue'],       # Highlight max values
   131	    highlight_min=['Growth'],        # Highlight min values
   132	    currency_cols=['Revenue'],       # Format as currency
   133	    percent_cols=['Growth'],         # Format as percent
   134	    align={'Region': 'left', 'Revenue': 'right'}
   135	)
   136	```
   137	
   138	#### Charts
   139	
   140	```python
   141	# Bar chart
   142	report.add_chart(
   143	    data=df,
   144	    chart_type="bar",
   145	    x="Region",
   146	    y="Revenue",
   147	    title="Revenue by Region"

   173	    y="Revenue",
   174	    title="Revenue Analysis",
   175	    color="#3498db",
   176	    width=6,           # inches

   178	    show_values=True,
   179	    show_legend=True
   180	)
   181	```
   182	
   183	#### Images
   184	
   185	```python
   186	# Add image
   187	report.add_image("screenshot.png", caption="Dashboard View")
   188	report.add_image("diagram.png", width=5, caption="Architecture Diagram")
   189	```
   190	
   191	#### Special Elements
   192	
   193	```python

   195	report.add_page_break()
   196	
   197	# Horizontal line
   198	report.add_divider()

   207	)
   208	
   209	# Quote
   210	report.add_quote(
   211	    "Data is the new oil.",
   212	    attribution="Clive Humby"
   213	)

   215	
   216	### Sections and Structure
   217	
   218	```python
   219	# Start a new section

   222	# Add content to section
   223	report.add_text("...")

1	# Active Satellites Currently In Orbit (2026)
     2	
     3	## About the Dataset
     4	
     5	This dataset is a real-time catalog of **14,875 active satellites** currently orbiting Earth, sourced from the **CelesTrak** space-tracking platform via **NORAD** Two-Line Element (TLE) data. It was published on Kaggle (`ibrahimqasimi/active-satellites-currently-in-orbit`) and covers the full range of operational spacecraft — from mega-constellations like Starlink to individual science missions, weather satellites, GPS navigation satellites, reconnaissance platforms, and the International Space Station.
     6	
     7	- **File:** `Active_Satellites_In_Orbit.csv`
     8	- **Rows:** 14,875
     9	- **Columns:** 17
    10	
    11	## Column Schema
    12	
    13	| Column Name | Type | Description |
    14	|---|---|---|
    15	| OBJECT_NAME | String | Satellite name (e.g., STARLINK-1234, ISS, GPS BIIR-2) |
    16	| OBJECT_ID | String | International designator in format YYYY-NNNXXX (launch year, launch number, piece letter). Useful for extracting launch year. |
    17	| EPOCH | String (datetime) | Date/time when the orbital element set was generated. Format: ISO 8601. Most entries are very recent. |
    18	| MEAN_MOTION | Float | Number of orbits per day. Key for orbit classification: >14 ≈ LEO, ~1.0 ≈ GEO, between ≈ MEO. |
    19	| ECCENTRICITY | String | Orbit shape factor (0 = perfectly circular, approaching 1 = highly elliptical). Stored as a string with leading decimal (e.g., ".002524"); needs conversion to float. |
    20	| INCLINATION | Float | Orbital tilt relative to the equator in degrees (0° = equatorial, 90° = polar). |
    21	| RA_OF_ASC_NODE | Float | Right ascension of the ascending node in degrees. |
    22	| ARG_OF_PERICENTER | Float | Argument of perigee in degrees. |
    23	| MEAN_ANOMALY | Float | Position of the satellite in its orbit at EPOCH, in degrees. |
    24	| EPHEMERIS_TYPE | Integer | Always 0 in standard TLE data. |
    25	| CLASSIFICATION_TYPE | String | Security classification ("U" = unclassified for most entries). |
    26	| NORAD_CAT_ID | Integer | Unique NORAD catalog number for each object. |
    27	| ELEMENT_SET_NO | Integer | Element set version number. |
    28	| REV_AT_EPOCH | Integer | Revolution (orbit) count at the time of EPOCH. |
    29	| BSTAR | String/Integer | Atmospheric drag coefficient (B* term). Stored in scientific notation as a string (e.g., ".64393E-3"); needs parsing. |
    30	| MEAN_MOTION_DOT | String | First derivative of mean motion (drag term). Stored as a string. |
    31	| MEAN_MOTION_DDOT | Integer | Second derivative of mean motion. Typically 0. |
    32	
    33	## Key Analysis Notes
    34	
    35	1. **Orbit Classification:** Use `MEAN_MOTION` to classify orbits. Satellites with >14 rev/day are in LEO (~160–2,000 km altitude). Those near 1.0 rev/day are in GEO (~35,786 km). Values between indicate MEO. Highly eccentric orbits (high `ECCENTRICITY`) with unusual mean motions may be HEO (e.g., Molniya orbits).
    36	
    37	2. **Constellation Identification:** The `OBJECT_NAME` field contains constellation prefixes (e.g., "STARLINK-", "ONEWEB-", "IRIDIUM", "GPS"). Parsing these prefixes enables grouping by operator/constellation.
    38	
    39	3. **Launch Year Extraction:** The first four characters of `OBJECT_ID` represent the launch year (e.g., "2024-" means launched in 2024). This enables temporal analysis of the active fleet.
    40	
    41	4. **Data Quality:** `ECCENTRICITY`, `BSTAR`, and `MEAN_MOTION_DOT` are stored as strings and require type conversion before numerical analysis. `MEAN_MOTION_DDOT` and `EPHEMERIS_TYPE` are nearly always 0 and carry little analytical value. No significant missing values are reported, but string-encoded scientific notation fields need careful parsing.
    42	
    43	5. **Starlink Dominance:** Approximately 6,000+ of the 14,875 satellites belong to SpaceX's Starlink constellation, which will heavily skew distributions unless filtered or segmented.
